sentences.text: Attenborosaurus is an extinct genus of pliosaurid, a type of marine reptile, that lived in the Early Jurassic in Dorset, England.
The holotype individual measured approximately 4.3 meters in length and is unusual for combining a relatively long neck with a relatively large head.
Skin impressions suggest the creature had membranous skin without large scales, likely an adaptation to reduce water resistance.
The genus name honors Sir David Attenborough, while the species name honors William Conybeare.
This piscivorous predator fed primarily on fish, a diet common among its contemporaries but notable for its specific specialization.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Charmouth, Dorset, England in 1880 and formally described in 1881.
The original holotype specimen was destroyed in November 1940 during World War II.
Originally described as Plesiosaurus conybeari by Sollas in 1881, the species was moved to the new genus Attenborosaurus by Bakker in 1993 based on studies of plaster casts.
Fossils of Attenborosaurus were found in Sinemurian strata in Charmouth, Dorset, England, indicating it lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
